summary: Feed s133_double is degraded: 100% of packets are untagged (required VLANs 10, 20 missing) and IDS port is severely overloaded with 2.79 Gbps bursts vs 1 Gbps capacity (279% overload).

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is stripping 802.1Q tags before delivery - 100% of frames arrive untagged so required VLANs 10 and 20 are never seen. Typically caused by broker ingress set to 'strip tags' or SPAN/monitor port configured as access instead of trunk passthrough.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS loses VLAN segmentation context it requires for VLANs 10 and 20 - cannot apply VLAN-aware policies, correlate assets, or detect cross-VLAN lateral movement, creating complete blind spot for those segments.

recommended_fix.why: Preserve 802.1Q tags end-to-end from TAP/SPAN through broker to IDS so required VLANs are visible for detection and policy enforcement.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate traffic is bursting to 2.79 Gbps in 1ms intervals and being forwarded to a single 1 Gbps IDS port (279% of capacity, 3 overloaded intervals). Broker has no load-balancing, filtering, or burst buffering, so microbursts overwhelm the tool.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS with 1 Gbps port will drop packets, fail flow reassembly and miss signatures despite needing full payload and both directions - overload directly causes detection gaps and evasion.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute flows across 2-3 IDS ports/instances with flow-aware hashing to keep each port <80% utilization while preserving bidirectional flow integrity required by IDS.
